biological_hypothesis: If clades specialize evolutionarily on the flower versus fruit signalling phase, clades retaining stronger flower-color memory should tend to retain weaker fruit-color memory, and vice versa.
relative_time_axis: pairwise patristic distance / (2 * source-tree crown height); source tree must have root-to-tip CV <= 1e-8

memory_curve.baseline: exact without-replacement same-state probability from retained state frequencies
memory_curve.primary_clade_metric: signed trapezoid area of excess-retention curve
memory_curve.secondary_clade_metric: linear slope of excess retention over relative divergence depth

primary_test.statistic: Spearman correlation of flower versus fruit signed excess-retention area across eligible clades

secondary_tests: Spearman correlation of flower versus fruit decay slopes, expected negative
leave-one-clade-out sign stability of the primary rho
descriptive count of flower-memory-dominant versus fruit-memory-dominant clades
claim_boundary: retrospective test; not independent of the published source study's flower-fruit lability tradeoff
memory metrics reuse the same color states and source trees but ask a relative-time persistence question
no pollinator-versus-disperser mechanism is identified directly
clade is the inferential replication unit
